name: Takeoff
summary: Planned quantities per stage and location: the denominator that measured work is compared against. Takeoff can be keyed in by hand, imported (Arth parser, Togal, upload), or absent in a non-takeoff project.

roles.note: The seed catalog has no takeoff-specific permission string. The docs list "Update takeoff" for admin and collaborator without naming the permission that enforces it (DEC-010).

nfr.statement: Largest takeoff import (elements per sheet, sheets per project) that must succeed.
nfr.open_question: What import sizes do customers send today, and what is the commitment?

nfr.statement: Time from a takeoff correction to recalculated historical percentages appearing in overview, trends and reports.
nfr.open_question: Is recalculation expected within seconds, or is a background job with a visible "recalculating" state acceptable?

requirements.title: Correcting a takeoff error recalculates past percentages
requirements.statement: When a takeoff change corrects an error, past completion percentages must be recalculated against the corrected quantity. Measured quantities on past dates stay as recorded. This does not set the policy for genuine scope changes (DEC-001) or for already-issued report files (DEC-004).

sources.title: Product walkthrough and clarifications recorded in the 2026-10-28 ledger

open_checks: No end-to-end test shows recalculated history propagating consistently to overview

acceptance_criteria.given: On a past date, 40 units were measured against an erroneous takeoff of 100
acceptance_criteria.then: That date's percentage becomes 50% wherever measured/takeoff is shown, and the measured quantity stays 40

requirements.title: Takeoff and progress carry forward to a revised design
requirements.statement: Today, when a revised design is activated, existing takeoff and progress carry forward to it. Whether this should remain the intended behaviour is an open question (DEC-003).

sources.title: Product walkthrough and clarifications recorded in the 2026-10-28 ledger

acceptance_criteria.given: A sheet with takeoff and recorded progress
acceptance_criteria.when: A revised design for that location is activated
acceptance_criteria.then: The existing takeoff and progress remain and apply to the revised design

requirements.title: Location takeoff is the sum of its active takeoff elements
requirements.statement: The planned quantity for a location, category and stage is the sum of that stage's quantity across the active takeoff elements. If none remain, it is zero.

sources.title: Track3D "Single Source of Truth" docs, generated from code

acceptance_criteria.given: Two active takeoff elements on a floor with 30 and 50 units of Drywall-Framing, and one doNotTrack element with 20

requirements.title: Denominator precedence, falling back to the measured value
requirements.statement: A percentage uses the takeoff keyed in by hand for the stage and location first, then imported takeoff. If neither exists, it uses the measured quantity itself, so the item shows as 100% complete.
requirements.rationale: The fallback is a defensive default in code, not a product decision. It conflicts with PROG-REQ-009.

sources.title: Track3D "Single Source of Truth" docs, generated from code

acceptance_criteria.given: A stage and location with 25 units measured and no takeoff keyed in or imported
acceptance_criteria.then: The denominator is 25 and the item shows 100%

requirements.title: Missing takeoff is surfaced and can be filled in
requirements.statement: In a takeoff project, when any stage in a location or category has no takeoff, users see a notice saying the value is missing and can enter the missing values from an update form.

dispute.summary: The PRD expects missing takeoff to be flagged. The code's fallback makes such items look 100% complete. Product must choose the intended behaviour (DEC-008).

sources.title: Track3D "Single Source of Truth" docs, generated from code

acceptance_criteria.given: A takeoff value is missing for a stage in a level or category
acceptance_criteria.when: The user views the progress details or overview page
acceptance_criteria.then: A notice tells the user the value is missing

acceptance_criteria.when: The user enters the missing value

acceptance_criteria.then: A form opens listing every missing value. Submitting it saves the values and confirms success.

requirements.title: Projects can be tracked without takeoff
requirements.statement: A progress project can run without takeoff. It is then tracked in absolute measured quantities, and percentage indicators are hidden. Users can switch a project between takeoff and non-takeoff views without losing data.

acceptance_criteria.given: A user is on a project page
acceptance_criteria.when: They switch between takeoff and non-takeoff mode
acceptance_criteria.then: The page reflects the selected mode and no data is lost
Values are shown as absolute quantities

requirements.title: Takeoff quantities are split across zones by coverage
requirements.statement: Each takeoff element's quantity is allocated to the zones of its structure in proportion to the share of the element each zone covers. If the geometry for one zone fails, that zone is skipped and the others are still saved.
requirements.rationale: This allocation does not itself enforce that zones never overlap. That rule (T3D-BR-036, gap T3D-GAP-011) moves with PROJ.

sources.title: Track3D "Single Source of Truth" docs, generated from code

acceptance_criteria.given: A 100-unit takeoff element, 60% inside zone A and 40% inside zone B
acceptance_criteria.then: Zone A receives 60 units and zone B receives 40
